text: In Genesis 22 a question is raised which the narrator leaves unanswered. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; and of what Abraham feels upon hearing the command we are told nothing, for the narrator gives no account of his inner life. He neither protests nor bargains. Of the man who once argued on behalf of Sodom there is here no trace whatever. Abraham appears to us less as a character than as a silence; and upon that silence the whole chapter turns.
